description:
Delete MapTag (types/sigs.rs:20) and its 23 tag-reading sites in the type kernel. A struct type is a record whose __struct__ field is the module's atom (%Pt{x: int} = %{__struct__: :"Elixir.Pt", x: int}); proven by a scratch kernel test, 14/14 identities, scratchpad proof/scratch_struct_field_encoding.patch. map_top is every map; the six callers meaning every map (resolve.rs:118, dispatch_reachability.rs:323, type_pred.rs:94, semantic.rs:617, :2444, types/mod.rs:521) widen with no change; the protocol target Map (world.rs:3138, module_impl_target_ty) becomes map_top \ %{__struct__: atom}, so protocols stay struct-first. The runtime predicate's struct axes (runtime_type_predicate.rs, types/mod.rs:3580) read __struct__ in either layout. StructTag's ModuleId dependency moves to struct_module_value_ty. Fixtures: is_map(p), case p do %{x: x}, MapSet unchanged, Enumerable miss on a struct, a Map.put-grown struct dispatching as its struct. Every moved pin reported with mechanism; none edited without authorization. Docs: set-theoretic-types.md, any-value.md, protocols.md, guides. Waits for S1 and for fz-sc8.99 to land (dispatch_matrix files).

Two gaps this ticket closes, both present on 6566a5765 and unchanged by S1: (1) Map.get(p, :__struct__) on a struct panics in run and build with "cannot coerce atom and numeric raw ABI reprs" (native_codegen/fn_ctx.rs:495); the cause is not field_lookup: a MapGet whose result type is an atom was lowered as a raw integer (native_codegen/prim.rs), so Map.get(%{x: :a}, :x) on a plain map panicked the same way. Interp prints Pt. (2) Map.get/3, Map.has_key?/2 and Map.merge/2 on a struct raise BadMapError on every path, because a 'map ::' clause guard does not admit a struct. Elixir answers :none, true and a merged map. Both become fixtures here once the struct type is a map type.

Layout after the tag goes (spike, 2026-11-12). Today the tag is what promises the struct layout: every value of a tagged type is a schema object. Without it the type says which struct a value is, not how it is laid out: a struct grown by Map.put, or `%{__struct__: Pt, x: 1, y: 2}` built as a plain map, has the same type and is in the entries layout. Three answers were weighed:
- (a) Chosen: the typed steps ask at run time (fz-3sy.17, lands directly beneath this ticket; the two PRs merge as a pair). Cost about 17 instructions per read and 15 per update compiled.
- (b) Dropped: keep a layout tag in the types. It keeps the concept this ticket exists to delete.
- (c) Dropped: a closed struct record plus one freeze-time normalisation of entries maps into struct layout. Not buildable as described: the kernel has only open records (`MapSig` means at least these keys), so a closed record is a new kind of type; and entries maps are published from several sites (alloc_map_slots, alloc_ordered_map_entries, publish_entries_in_place, map_put_entry, static literals), not one freeze.

Fixtures this ticket owes for fz-3sy.17's entries side, each against elixir on interp, run and build: a struct grown by Map.put then read through a typed step; the same grown struct through a typed update; `%{__struct__: Pt, x: 1, y: 2}` built as a plain map then read with `.x`.

Build findings (2026-11-13).
- A map literal that writes no __struct__ key is typed record ∧ plain_map (Types::map_literal), plain_map = map_top \ %{__struct__: atom}. Without it a protocol call on a literal map is no longer resolved at compile time and the inventory and body-walk pins rise.
- Key widening (widen_literals, the convergence collapse of map values) leaves the __struct__ field alone. Widening it made Enumerable.Range.count's input demand a new question on fixture 00420 and moved three pins; with the field kept, no pin moves.
- refine_widen and pattern substitution merge only records naming the same module.
- The run-time predicate's other-structs axis follows the tuple axis's top, so a tuple does not pass a map guard (fixture 00616).
- Runtime: Heap::named_schema answers NamedSchema::{None, Schema, Undeclared} for either layout; a MAP-kind value is tested on the maps and named-structs axes by the module it names; native reads it through fz_map_named_schema_ref.
- The interpreter's two by-name field reads fold into fz_struct_get_named_field_ref.
- Not here: cross-layout == and printing an entries map as %Name{...} are fz-3sy.3. lib/map.fz has no Map.from_struct/1.
- Fixtures: 00861, 00862, 00863.
title: A struct is a map type: MapTag goes
